exclusion_detail: The starting material, curcumol, is an isolated plant natural product with no purchase statement, and the 4-step count needs a telescoped epoxidation/ring-opening (second reader: reject). (Reclassified 2026-10-24 after the verification pass.)

lead.label: 13t
lead.why: Abstract: 'Among them, 13t with a 4-fluorophenyl demonstrated the most potent dose-dependent inhibition of GBM cell viability, providing a novel lead compound'.

reactions.conditions: (i) mCPBA (2 equiv), CH2Cl2, rt, 2 h; quench with aq. Na2S2O3, extract, crude epoxide used directly; (ii) NaOH (3 equiv), iPrOH, 70 C, 2 h; silica chromatography; 56 % over the two steps.
reactions.source: Main text p.2 and SI 'Synthesis of 10'

reactions.conditions: Dess-Martin periodinane (1.5 equiv), NaHCO3 (2 equiv), CH2Cl2, 0 C to rt, 6 h; 78 %.
Pinnick: NaClO2 (1.4 equiv), NaH2PO4 (0.3 equiv), 30 % H2O2, MeCN/H2O, rt, overnight; acidify with 2 N HCl and filter; 93 %.
HATU (1.2 equiv), amine (1.1 equiv), MeCN, rt, overnight; silica chromatography; 91 % for 13t.

alt_variants.conditions: mCPBA (2 equiv), CH2Cl2, rt, 2 h; Na2S2O3 quench; crude, not characterised.

notes: CHECK: (1) The paper counts the route as 'four-step' and gives one procedure and one two-step yield for curcumol -> 10 (epoxidation then NaOH ring opening with only a work-up between, epoxide never isolated); I count it as one step per the telescoped-sequence rule, so 4 steps; as two separate reactions it would be 5 (second variant lists steps 1-2 of that reading, steps 3-5 are the same as above). (2) Curcumol is not printed with a structure or name anywhere in the text and the paper does not say it is purchased or isolated; I derived its SMILES (exocyclic 8-methylene guaiane hemiketal, C15H24O2) from product 10 (C15H24O3, allylic CH2OH, ring CH=) and from my knowledge of curcumol; the spiro-epoxide of the methylene opened by base to the endocyclic allylic alcohol explains 10. The SI title says 'Curcumenol' although the paper says curcumol, and the SI's mass/mmol of curcumol (2.36 g, 6.7 mmol) does not match curcumol's molar mass. (3) Main text swaps labels once (says 13s = 4-fluorophenyl and 13t = 4-bromophenyl), but abstract, conclusion and SI all give 13t = 4-fluorophenyl and 13s = 4-bromophenyl. (4) Stereodescriptors are in the printed name only; the SMILES are flat. 4-Fluoroaniline is not named in the paper; inferred from the 13t name (no doubt). NaClO2 oxygen not listed as an atom-supplying reagent.
